messages:
anya: quick heads-up — hit a p99 spike during last night's cutover from microbatch -> continuous on a small subset of tenants. suspect the batch cutover handshake is stalling inflight KV cache lookups.

matt: ugh. any stack traces or sample logs?

anya: here's the pattern i see in logs:
```
[23:11:02] enqueue req id=abc lane=low -> placed in pending
[23:11:02] scheduler: build batch b1 includes id=abc, cutoff_marker=none
[23:11:02] executor: flush start batch b1, sees missing kv for id=abc -> fetch block
[23:11:03] scheduler: cutover request -> attempt to switch to continuous lane
[23:11:03] executor: blocked on kv fetch, batch b1 waiting, new requests appended to continuous queue
[23:11:05] p99 spike observed for id=abc (2s)
```

li: that makes sense. current contract assumes executor can accept a `cutover_marker` and atomically switch the batch envelope. but we never guaranteed the executor won't be mid-fetch.

sarah: is this more of an admission problem (we let too many items into the old envelope) or a cutover ordering problem (switch executed behind a blocked op)?

anya: ordering. the scheduler issued a cutover while an executor goroutine was blocked on I/O. we don't have a reliable handoff to drain that goroutine before starting the new continuous batch.

rajesh: options: A) serial handoff (block cutover until all in-flight execs finish) B) steal-and-requeue (executor returns partially processed items to scheduler) C) soft-cutover (start new lane but keep old executor draining until timeout)

matt: A might be safe but kills latency. B needs requeue semantics + idempotency. C seems pragmatic: set a short drain window and fallback to requeue on timeout.

li: agree. also need clearer executor <-> scheduler API. propose adding a small rpc: `BatchHandoff{batch_id, soft_deadline_ns, resume_token?}`. executor returns `HandoffAck{drained_count, pending_items[], state_token}`.

anya: proto sketch:
```proto
message BatchHandoff {
  string batch_id = 1;
  int64 soft_deadline_ns = 2; // how long executor should try to finish
  bool force_requeue = 3; // scheduler hint
}
message HandoffAck {
  string batch_id = 1;
  repeated string requeue_ids = 2;
  bytes state_token = 3; // optional opaque state for resume
}
```

sarah: we should avoid opaque tokens if possible — they complicate observability. maybe just return counters + requeue list.

rajesh: also add metrics: `cutover_attempts`, `cutover_failures`, `cutover_drain_time_ms`, `requeued_count`. we can alert on cutover_failures>0.5% for 10m.

matt: what about the queue boundary refactor we talked about last sprint? if we make lane boundaries explicit at enqueue time with `lane_hint` and `lane_stability_ttl`, scheduler wouldn't need to move items between queues as much. reduces cutovers.

li: hmm lane_stability_ttl helps for bursty clients but we still need cutovers for global policy changes (cost routing, regional fallback).

anya: thought: combine both. allow a `preferred_lane` at enqueue, and require any scheduler-initiated lane migration to use the handoff protocol. by default items stick to preferred_lane for X seconds.

matt: sample enqueue snippet:
```json
{"req_id":"abc","preferred_lane":"low","lane_stability_s":10}
```

sarah: for migration semantics: when scheduler wants to move an item, it sends `Handoff` to the executor responsible for that batch. executor has `soft_deadline` window to either finish or return `requeue_ids`. scheduler then either re-enqueues or lets new lane pick them up.

li: make sure to define invariants: 1) at-most-once in-flight execution per request id 2) if requeued, must preserve prior KV/cache validity or trigger fresh fetch with upstream trace info 3) metrics + span for cutover path

rajesh: edge case: what if executor process dies during drain? scheduler should detect via liveness probe and immediately requeue all pending items for that batch. record `cutover_failures++`.

anya: agree. also want a fallback mode: if >10% of cutovers fail in a minute, revert to conservative mode where we avoid lane migrations for 5m. (circuit-breaker)

matt: implementation plan:
- add `preferred_lane` and `lane_stability_s` to enqueue API (devex + SDK changes)
- implement `BatchHandoff` rpc and `HandoffAck` in runtime protocol
- add metrics + tracing for cutover path
- canary: enable on 1% traffic for dedicated clusters, watch `cutover_drain_time_ms` and p99

li: timeline? can do proto+metrics in 1 sprint, executor changes + SDK in 2. canary start early next sprint.

sarah: quick UX note for devex: document that `preferred_lane` is a hint and migrations may still happen for policy reasons. show example for low-latency vs low-cost lanes.

anya: last question — requeue semantics: should requeued items preserve original enqueue timestamp (for fairness)?

matt: yes, keep original ts but add a `migrated_from` field so quota/ordering logic can account for churn.

li: also add `requeue_retries` to avoid hot loops. increment on each requeue and cap at 3.

rajesh: i'll draft an RFC follow-up with the proto and metric names + rollback plan. ping @anya for logs and a short dump of affected tenants.

anya: sending logs now. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: Deploy started for branch `cutover-handshake-v1` -> canary on ded-1 cluster (1%).

matt: nice, will watch dashboards.

(END)
